FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Flooring, 
Wall Finishing and Roofing Sectional Committee had been approved by the Civil Engineering Division Council. 


Aluminium composite panel (ACP) consists of three main layers, that is top and bottom coated aluminium sheet 
and in between a core material made either of low-density polyethylene (LDPE) or mineral based material. The 
core is connected to top and bottom coated aluminium sheet by adhesive films. 


ACP may be intended for external applications such as cladding fagades, curtain walls, soffits, canopy and 
high masts; those intended for internal use, such as partitions, ceilings, column encasement; those for use in 
transportation related applications like railway coach furnishings; and fire-retardant ACP with a wide range of 
properties appropriate to the type of application. These panels may have either smooth or textured surface. 


This standard covers the physical, mechanical, coating and fire-retardant properties for flat aluminium composite 
panel (ACP). Other requirements related to acoustic and thermal properties have been also given, for which ACP 
shall comply to the same on demand of the purchaser. 


The composition of the Committee responsible for the in the formulation of this standard is given in Annex D. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with the final value, 
observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis shall be rounded off in accordance with 
IS 2 : 1960 “Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised )’. The number of significant places retained in the 
rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 


IS 17682 : 2021 


Indian Standard 


ALUMINIUM 
COMPOSITE PANEL — SPECIFICATION 


1SCOPE 


This standard covers the requirements for flat aluminium 
composite panel (ACP) intended for external applications, 
such as cladding fagades, curtain walls, soffits, canopy 
and high mast monolith; those intended for internal use, 
such as partitions, ceilings and column encasement; 
those for use in transportation related application like 
railway coach furnishing; and fire-retardant ACP with 
a wide range of properties appropriate to the type of 
application. 


2 REFERENCE 


The Indian standards given in Annex A contain provisions 
which through reference in this text, constitute provisions 
of this standard. At the time of publication, the editions 
indicated were valid. All standards are subject to revision, 
and parties to agreements based on this standard are 
encouraged to investigate the possibility of applying the 
most recent editions of the standards indicated in Annex 
A. 


3 TERMINOLOGY 


For the purpose of this standard, the following definitions 
shall apply. 


3.1 Aluminium Composite Panel (ACP)/Aluminium 
Composite Material (ACM) — A flat panel consisting 
of three main layers, that is top and bottom coated 
aluminium sheet and in between a core material made 
either of low density polyethylene (LDPE) or mineral 
based material. The core is connected to top and bottom 
coated aluminium coil by adhesive films. 


3.2 Base Metal Thickness (BMT) — The thickness of 
top and bottom layer of aluminum sheet without coating. 


3.3 LDPE Core ACP — An ACP consisting of 
homogeneous, non-toxic, antioxidant thermoplastic low 
density polyethylene (LDPE) core laminated and bonded 
with top and bottom adhesive film to coated layers of 
aluminium sheets of required thickness. The core 
shall be of LDPE or a mix of LDPE and high density 
polyethylene (HDPE). 


3.4 Mineral Core ACP — An ACP consisting of 
homogeneous mixture of inorganic content either 
magnesium hydroxide or aluminium trihydrate with 
LDPE and admixtures to form the core, laminated and 
bonded with top and bottom adhesive film to coated 
layers of aluminium sheets of required thickness. 


4 CLASSIFICATION 


ACP shall be classified as follows, with thickness of all 
external grade ACP being equal to and greater than 4 
mm and of all internal grade ACP being less than 4 mm: 


a) Grade 1 (External Grade LDPE Core ACP) — 
These are LDPE core ACP intended for external 
applications where they may be subjected to the 
direct action of sun, rain, wind or snow. These 
shall have top and bottom aluminium BMT of 
minimum 0.5 mm. 


Grade 2 (Internal Grade LDPE Core ACP) — 
These are LDPE core ACP intended for internal 
applications where they will not be subjected to 
the direct action of sun, rain, wind or snow. These 
shall have top and bottom aluminium BMT of 
minimum 0.25 mm. 


Grade 2S (Signage Grade LDPE Core 
ACP) — ACP of thickness less than 4 mm which 
has LDPE core ACP intended for applications 
(like signage application) where they are directly 
exposed to the weather (like direct action of sun, 
rain, wind or snow). These shall have top and 
bottom aluminium BMT of minimum 0.3 mm 
with Polyvinylidene Fluoride or Polyvinylidene 
difluoride (PVDF)/Super Durable Polyester 
(SDP)/Fluoroethylene Vinyl Ether (FEVE) 
coating. 

Grade 3 (External Grade Mineral Core Fire 
Retardant ACP) — These are the mineral core 
ACP which can withstand when subjected to 
higher temperatures during an incident of fire. 
These shall have top and bottom aluminium BMT 
minimum 0.5 mm. 


Grade 4 (Internal Grade Mineral Core Fire 
Retardant ACP) — These are the mineral core 
ACP which can withstand when subjected to 
higher temperatures during an incident of fire. 
These shall have top and bottom aluminium BMT 
minimum 0.25 mm. 


f) Grade 5 (Mineral Core Fire Retardant ACP for 
High Rise and Special Buildings) — ACP of 
thickness equal to and greater than 4 mm which 
has mineral core and withstand when subjected 
to higher temperatures during an incident of fire 
in high rise and special buildings mentioned in 
SP 7 (Part 4). These shall have top and bottom 
aluminium BMT minimum 0.5 mm.

NOTE — Grade 1, Grade 2 and Grade 2S shall not be preferred 
for building façade, habitat area (where there is a chance of fire 
hazards) façade and in transportation vehicles, like railway and 
bus coaches etc. 


5 MATERIALS 


5.1 Polymer Granules 


Low density polyethylene (LDPE) and high density 
polyethylene (HDPE) shall have melt flow index of 
0.5 to 2 g/10 min when tested as per IS 2530. These 
shall be homogeneous and monolithic non-toxic 
thermoplastic polyethylene. The ash content of the 
LDPE and HDPE shall not be more than 10 percent 
when tested as per IS 12235 (Part 17). 


5.2 Aluminium Alloy Sheets 


The aluminium alloy sheets used in manufacturing 
of ACP shall be of designations 19002 or 31500B or 
51000A with conditions H x 6 or H x 8, conforming to 
IS 737. 


5.3 Adhesive 
It shall be polyolefin type or as agreed between the 
manufacturer and purchaser. The placement method 
may be any of the following: 

a) Co-extrusion with the polymer core, 

b) Lamination with a pre-made film, or 


c) Extrusion coating on the polymer core layer. 


5.4 Surface Coating 


The coating on top aluminium sheets shall be 
done with polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) with 
(70:30 PVDF:acrylic ratio) or fluoroethylene 
vinyl ether (FEVE) or polyester resin based paints 
and bottom aluminium sheet shall be coated with 
anti-corrosive paint. 


5.4.1 Protective coating shall be used, as follows: 

a) Polyester — For Grade 2 product category. 

b) Super Durable Polyester (SDP) — For Grade 2, 
Grade 3, Grade 4, Grade 5 and Grade 2S product 
categories. 

c) Polyvinylidene Fluoride (PVDF) — For Grade 1, 
Grade 2, Grade 2S, Grade 3 Grade 4 and Grade 5 
product categories. 

d) Fluoroethylene Vinyl Ether (FEVE) — For Grade 
1, Grade 2S, Grade 3, Grade 4 and Grade 5 product 
categories. 


6 DIMENSIONS AND TOLERANCE 


6.1 The nominal dimensions of ACP shall be as follows: 
a) 1 200 mm x 2 400 mm; 
b) 1200 mm x 3 050 mm; and 
c) 1200 mm x 3 660 mm. 


6.2 Thickness 


The nominal thickness of ACP shall be 2 mm, 3 mm, 
4 mm, 5 mm and 6 mm. 


NOTE — Any other dimensions (length, width and thickness) 
as agreed to between the manufacturer and the purchaser may 
also be used. 


6.3 Tolerances 


Tolerance on the nominal sizes of finished boards shall 
be as given in Table 1.

8.1.1 Lot of Coated Aluminium Sheet Coil 


Aluminium sheet coil of same grade manufactured

8.1.2 Lot of ACP 

ACP of same grade manufactured under similar

Three samples of size 1.10 m x 1.10 m, shall be drawn 
at random from a lot and shall be subjected to tests as 
per 6 and 7. If any sample fails to conform to any of 


to the requirements specified in this standard. 


9 INFORMATION TO BE PROVIDED BY THE 
MANUFACTURER 


9.1 The manufacturer shall, upon request, furnish the 
purchaser or his representative with the test certificate 
showing conformity of the product to this standard in 
all respects. 


9.2 Information to User 


The manufacturer shall, through its distribution system, 
supply adequate information to the users concerning 
safety precautions to be taken during handling or 
machining of products and that exposure to dust 


by cutting, drilling, sanding and turning or similar 
operations should be avoided by one or more of the 
following means: 


a) Using low speed power tools, 


b) Using personal protective equipment (respirators), 
and 


c) Use of manual-tools. 
10 MARKING 


10.1 Each ACP shall be legibly and indelibly marked 
with the following information: 


a) Indication of source of the manufacture; 


IS 17682 : 2021 


b) Length, width and thickness of ACP; 
c) Grade of ACP; 

d) Coating type; and 

e) Batch no. and date of manufacture. 


10.2 BIS Certification Marking 


The product(s) conforming to the requirements of 
this standard may be certified as per the conformity 
assessment schemes under the provisions of the 
Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 and the Rules 
and Regulations framed thereunder, and the products 
may be marked with the Standard Mark.

ANNEX B 
(Table 1) 
METHOD FOR MEASURMENT OF DIMENSIONS OF ACP 


A-1 APPARATUS 


Apparatus shall include measuring tape with 
accuracy of 1 mm and for thickness digital vernier 
caliper/micro-meter with accuracy of 0.001 mm. 


A-2 MEASUREMENT 


length and width shall be measure to the nearest | mm 
using a measuring tape at least two places one at middle 
and one near the edge, and the same are reported. 


The thickness shall be measured to the nearest 0.001 mm 
at four edges and at two random spots in the middle of 
the panel using a vernier caliper/micro-meter, and the 
same shall be reported. 


Three samples ACP of each grade and size 

shall be taken for measuring dimensions. The 
ANNEX C 
(Table) 


METHOD FOR DETERMINATION OF EDGE STRAIGHTNESS AND SQUARENESS OF ACP 


B-1PROCEDUREFOREDGESTRAIGHTNESS 


The straightness of the edges and ends of ACP shall 
be verified against a straight edge not less than the full 
length of the ACP. If the edge on the end of the ACP is 
convex, it shall be held against the straightness edge in 
such a way as to give approximately equal gap at each 
end, the largest gap between the straight edge and the 
edge shall be measured to the nearest millimetre and 
recorded. 


B-2 PROCEDURE FOR SQUARENESS 


The squareness of ACP shall be checked with a 
1 200 mm x 1 200 mm square, by applying one arm of 
the square to the ACP. The maximum width of the gap 
shall be recorded on the other arm.

Bureau of Indian Standards 


BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 to promote harmonious 
development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods and attending to 
connected matters in the country. 


Copyright 


BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part ofthese publications may be reproduced in any form without 
the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of implementing the 
standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. Enquiries relating to 
copyright be addressed to the Director (Publications), BIS. 


Review of Indian Standards 


Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of 
“BIS Catalogue” and “Standards: Monthly Additions’. 


This Indian Standard has been developed from Doc No.: CED 05 (15898).
